title: Ethyl acetate + ethanol + water, NRTL, 10 stages: a second liquid on stages 5 to 10 only
purpose: Two liquids on some stages only, in a ternary (milestone M2b): stages 1 to 4 hold one liquid (near the ternary azeotrope, rich in ethyl acetate), stages 5 to 10 a second, water-rich liquid whose share falls from 25 % at the reboiler to under 2 % on stage 9 and rises again on the feed stage. Unlike a binary, the two-liquid stages are not invariant: their temperatures and liquid compositions change from stage to stage.
method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rules 3 and 7: polar, below 10 bar, two liquids possible: NRTL, the default sets of the three pairs (each fitted to measured data: ethanol + water, Kamihama et al. 2012; water + ethyl acetate, Grande et al. 2005 and others; ethanol + ethyl acetate, Calvar et al. 2005; src/data/binaries.json), ideal-gas vapour. The benchmark process "ethyl acetate with a decanter" (docs/BENCHMARKS.md) uses this system.

behaviour: two liquids on stages 5 to 10 and one liquid on stages 1 to 4 (fixture rigorous, each stage's `liquids`)
with phases "VL" the column is refused with PHASE_SPLIT naming stages where a second liquid forms
expected.branch: The reference's solution from its stated start. One solution expected; the engine's stages with two liquids must be the same.

engine_against_reference.why: Proposal 0015, Engineering basis: flows within 1e-6 relative of the independent MESH solution. Both solve the same equations to residuals of 1e-8 or less, so the difference is the solvers' convergence only.

balances_on_every_stage.why: Proposal 0015: every stage's balances closed to 1e-8. Material: |residual| / F; energy: |residual| / (F x 10 kJ/mol); summation and equilibrium are mole fractions.

stability.why: one-liquid stages: no trial liquid on a grid has a tangent-plane distance below -1e-9

agreement_with_data.note: The three NRTL sets are fitted to vapour-liquid data; their liquid-liquid split is W1's work (joint fits, M2b) and not a test of the column.
